claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with min D=3, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=11/6, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, all sufficiently large integers are sums of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with min D=3, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=11/6, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, all sufficiently large integers are sums of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite labelled subsets of positive-integer pure-power supplies, with elementary integer arithmetic and ordered subset sums.

shape.objects: Every input D is a finite rigid integer set with minimum three; k and finite labelled deletion F vary without bound; witnesses are finite subsets of pairs of natural numbers. These have standard Finset, product, power and gcd definitions in Lean/Mathlib. Disjoint finite supports have common extensions by union, and interval witnesses may be reached by iterating disjoint two-choice gadgets and adjoining a separate infinite reserve. Finite supports can be encoded as random variables, but no spread condition is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such finite D, every positive integer k and every finite labelled deletion F, there exists N(D,k,F), for every integer n>=N there is a finite subset of the remaining labels whose values sum to n. The leading quantifiers are universal over finite or countable arithmetic objects, with existential finite representation witnesses, not over sets of reals.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-representability property at the fixed stated reciprocal threshold, not an extremal numerical optimization or a density upper bound. An unspecified N(D,k,F) settles the claim.
shape.ambient_structure: Exact integer arithmetic and the order of the power values coexist. Balanced ternary is a known signed-digit tool; finite unit groups modulo powers of three supply congruences. Disjoint union and fresh-tail recursion are the proposed amplifying operations. No structured/random dichotomy, pairwise probabilistic overlap parameter, or proved category transport is recorded.
shape.symmetries: Base ordering and relabelling do not affect legal sums. Base addition, lowering the cutoff and removing fewer labels preserve any represented set, subject to keeping the stated input hypotheses. Arbitrary translation or dilation need not preserve the labelled pure-power supplies. No density-increment system of invariant pieces is recorded.
shape.configuration: Every n beyond an input-dependent threshold must be an exact positive sum of distinct remaining labels, with equal numerical values separately available. Proposed signed unit identities must be converted to two disjoint positive alternatives and successive gadgets must have disjoint supports. Restricting bases can remove three or b and destroy gcd, reciprocal mass and the seed; untracked deletion or truncation can also destroy a selected interval.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal construction or optimal threshold is asserted. The candidate is a finite interval on bases three and b coprime to three, together with the other bases as a disjoint syndetic reserve.
shape.finite_certificates: For each fixed D,k,F, an interval of the reserve's finite gap length with one finite labelled representation per point is a finite positive certificate once the analytical reserve lemma is proved. The elementary two-choice motif has positive gain one; finite motifs and arithmetic identities are directly checkable. No uniform finite global residue or bounded run is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: Yes: adding bases, lowering a positive cutoff or deleting fewer labels enlarges the represented set when the input hypotheses remain valid. The smallest positive cutoff is one, but all positive cutoffs are part of this claim, and cutoff-one examples do not settle them.
shape.uniformity_parameter: The positive cutoff k, finite deletion F, choice and number of bases D and eventual integer n are unbounded. N may depend on D,k,F. No common effective or ineffective N across inputs is required.
shape.proof_shape: A self-contained analytical candidate in moves/001-ternary-reserve.md proves the fixed-gap disjoint amplification, finite fresh-unit iteration, balanced-ternary tail identity, labelled prefix mesh and geometric reserve bound, then the exact all-cutoff threshold. Every introduced lemma is proved in the same move. No claim weakening, uniformity change or mathematical process is used. Independent result review is pending.
shape.neighbours: Known true: classical balanced ternary existence with digits minus one, zero and one; the finite interval plus disjoint syndetic reserve implication in the accepted mass proof; and the accepted13/4 high-mass result for minimum three. The all-cutoff root at mass one and the subclass below11/6 remain open. The generic inference from tail signed units and the previously recorded abstract profile to completeness was refuted in erdos-124-signed-tail-seed; it cannot replace the independent reserve. Finite candidate strengthenings can be checked symbolically. No simpler ambient carrying this exact claim verbatim, reflecting categorical equivalence, independent axiom variant or solved countable/uncountable split is recorded.

The present seed route has not yet been executed. The old three-group construction stops short of the new target, but no universal ceiling for counting, direct invariants or density increments in this exact special case is documented here. No first-moment estimate, uniform N independent of the input, finite complete residue or long stagnation of this new route is recorded.

A correct arithmetic or Lean check would stay within this base theory, but no such process is admitted.
